market_pulse.note: Closed Friday at about 52,347, up 0.1%, the only one of the three major U.S. indexes to finish higher (Kiplinger; 24/7 Wall St.).
Closed Friday at about 7,561, down 0.4%, recovering from a midday drop of nearly 1% but still posting a weekly gain (Kiplinger; 24/7 Wall St.).
Closed Friday at about 25,136, down 0.9%, as semiconductor stocks sold off for a second day; the index still ended the week higher (Kiplinger).
The December contract settled at $88.56 a barrel, down 0.2%, while Brent for January added 2 cents to $95.84 and notched a second weekly decline (Rigzone).

themes.title: Wholesale inflation stays hot
themes.summary: October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, below the 0.4% forecast, but were up 6.5% from a year earlier; core producer prices rose 5% annually, the most since January 2023 (Kiplinger; Yahoo Finance).

themes.title: Chip stocks lead the decline
themes.summary: AMD fell 8.8%, the worst performer in the S&P 500, while Broadcom lost 4.8%, Intel 2.5% and Nvidia 2%, as fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continued (Kiplinger).

themes.title: December rate-hike bets firm up
themes.summary: Futures traders put the probability of a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December at 90%, and the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17% during the day, its highest since October (Kiplinger; Yahoo Finance).

themes.title: A winning week despite Friday's slide
themes.summary: All three major benchmarks finished the week with gains even after Friday's losses, with the Dow edging higher on the day as money rotated out of technology (Kiplinger; 24/7 Wall St.).

themes.title: Oil eases on supply signals
themes.summary: Crude prices were little changed Friday; rising U.S. inventories, record seasonal refinery runs and an IEA forecast of a surplus this quarter weighed on prices, while attacks on Gulf shipping kept supply risk in view (Rigzone).

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.note: The weakest group, with AMD down 8.8%, Broadcom down 4.8%, Intel down 2.5% and Nvidia down 2% at the close (Kiplinger).

sectors.name: Networking and Hardware
sectors.note: Cisco fell 6.2% despite a beat-and-raise quarter, Fabrinet fell 7.9% and Dell Technologies fell 7.2% (Kiplinger; 24/7 Wall St.).

sectors.name: Defensive Sectors
sectors.note: Utilities led gains, with consumer staples up 0.7% and communication services up 0.4% as of mid-morning, while technology was down 2.8% (24/7 Wall St.).

sectors.name: Consumer and Software Gainers
sectors.note: Dutch Bros rose 6.7%, Duolingo 5.2% and AppLovin 3.9%, among the day's top gainers (24/7 Wall St.).

watch_list.why: Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close, its first results since Jensen Huang's departure; interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to speak on the call (Kiplinger).

Pricing is expected Wednesday evening with Nasdaq trading under "ANT" on Thursday; the company plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, and the offering is reportedly about six times oversubscribed (Kiplinger).
Markets are pricing a likely quarter-point rate hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting after this week's inflation data (Kiplinger; TheStreet).
